No. At six people, microservices will cost you more than they return. You'd take on distributed-systems overhead (service discovery, network failures, distributed tracing, cross-service transactions, per-service CI/CD and deploys, data consistency) without the organizational problem they exist to solve: many teams blocked on each other in one codebase. With six engineers, coordination is cheap and the monolith is your advantage.

What to do instead: make the monolith modular (clear domain boundaries, packwerk or engines to enforce them, no cross-domain table access), and scale it with ordinary tools: background jobs, caching, read replicas, query fixes. That keeps extraction possible later at low cost.

Cases where extracting one piece is justified: a component with very different scaling or resource needs (e.g., video processing, ML inference), a hard compliance isolation requirement, or a part needing a different language or runtime. Extract that single piece, not everything.

What would change my answer: if you have a concrete pain such as deploy times, test suite duration, or one hot path taking down the whole app, that's worth naming. Most of those have cheaper fixes than a rewrite, but I can't judge without knowing what's actually hurting.
